rationale: Block 3 introduces the core DSM-5 criteria for ADHD (inattentive / hyperactive-impulsive / combined) and ASD (two-domain: social communication + restricted/repetitive). This item checks recall of the minimum symptom-duration and age-of-onset requirements for ADHD — a pair of facts students frequently confuse (12 months vs 12 years, 6 symptoms vs 6 months).

Block 5 covers psychopathology and aetiology, including the common misconception that ADHD and ASD cannot co-occur. The DSM-5 explicitly removed the exclusion criterion, allowing dual diagnosis — a clinically critical point that block 11 (clinical_pearl) also highlights. Placing this TrueFalse after block 5 (before the clinical_pearl) reinforces the concept mid-SDL.

Block 8 covers management of ADHD and ASD, including first-line pharmacotherapy (methylphenidate for ADHD) and the absence of disease-modifying pharmacotherapy for ASD. This item presents a clinical scenario requiring students to apply treatment guidelines — higher Bloom level than the Remember/Understand items above, and not covered by the existing practice questions which focus on whether medication 'reverses' ASD.

Block 3 introduces the clinical definition of IDD, emphasising that DSM-5 severity is based on adaptive functioning, NOT IQ score alone. This is the single most commonly examined and clinically misapplied concept in IDD — reinforcing it immediately after the definitional block prevents the error from taking root.

Block 5 covers the aetiological framework (genetic, prenatal, perinatal, postnatal). This item asks students to identify the most common preventable postnatal cause of IDD — a distinct angle not covered by the existing Down syndrome practice question, testing application of the aetiological classification to a preventive medicine context.

Block 8 covers multidisciplinary management of IDD, including the key principle that no pharmacotherapy reverses the disability itself. This clinical vignette asks students to prioritise the correct first-line management action, distinguishing among the three components of multidisciplinary care — not covered by the existing practice question which asks about counselling on pharmacotherapy.
